name: e6-pitch-eff
airframe: Fighter1, Multirole1, SmallFighter1, trainer, VTOLTrainer1, CAS1, COIN, EW1, FastBomber1, Darkreach
note: THE PITCH-EFFECTIVENESS LATCH, ARMED - the highest-priority card on this slate and the best-supported mechanism anyone has produced for the maintainer standing 'it feels unresponsive' report. WHAT IS ARMED: Control/PitchEffRelax (header field pEffRelax=0/1). _pitchEff else-branch is a hard LATCH, not a floor - Max(_pitchEff, PEffRevThresh) returns exactly _pitchEff for any value above the threshold, so the filter update becomes += k*0. The measurement gate (|cmd| > 0.05) is open on only 5.3 pct of rows, so the estimator freezes a transient LAG sample and holds it for ~95 pct of every flight; pEff < 0.95 on 97.4 pct of rows. Downstream pErrTerm *= _pitchEff, so the law runs fixed-wing pitch demand at 0.47-0.80 of what it computed, permanently. Arm B relaxes toward 1 when there is no command to measure against. Evidence base: 48,085 rows, 10 airframes, oblique-6-c R44, zero flights. GEOMETRY IS ob-dwell-2, NOT oblique-6-c, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE CHOICE. oblique-6-c has the most baseline in the corpus, but it also has the dilution: 73.4 pct of its rows sit below the 0.5 deg azTR cut-off and 72-80 pct below the elevation equivalent, so an arm flown on it moves ~1 sample in 4 and every effect size is quartered before it is measured. ob-dwell-2 parks the loop at |azErr| and |elevErr| ~2.25 deg for the whole of every leg, i.e. 100 pct engagement, and its |aimRate| 3.54 deg/s clears the 3 deg/s _settleOK gate so the B2 settle path is out of the way. Same ten airframes, same 0.95x-corner entry, same pins - so ob-dwell-2 flown unarmed is this card direct control and MUST be in the same batch. REQUIREMENT 1, THE DIRECTION SPLIT - CUT BY LEG, NEVER POOL. The latch is direction-dependent: R44 pEff DOWN vs UP is 0.466/0.715 (Multirole1), 0.520/0.738 (SmallFighter1), 0.559/0.723 (COIN), 0.576/0.696 (trainer), 0.656/0.773 (Fighter1) - and it INVERTS on FastBomber1 (0.799/0.773) and Darkreach (0.845/0.706). Pooling DOWN and UP dilutes toward null and hides the inversion. This geometry emits two DOWN tags (obDR2pe, obDL2pe) and two UP tags (obUL2pe, obUR2pe), compare-runs.py keys segments by tag alone, and repeat 9 gives 8 scored replicates per lane = 4 per arm = 8 segments per DIRECTION per arm per airframe. That is the split, and it costs nothing extra. REQUIREMENT 2, LEGS ARE NOT INDEPENDENT WITHIN A CAPTURE, and the design handles it three ways rather than pretending otherwise. _pitchEff carries into every leg from the one before - the arm window itself latches ~0.749 on oblique-6-c before the first scored leg. (a) THE SLOT CONFOUND IS BROKEN BY GEOMETRY: this card alternates DOWN, UP, DOWN, UP (slots 1-4), so each direction gets one early and one late slot, where oblique-6-c runs down, down, up, up and confounds direction with position outright. (b) THE ARM CONTRAST IS UNAFFECTED BY IT ANYWAY: whatever the carry-over is, it is identical in structure on both arms, and ABBA over 8 scored replicates lands session drift on both equally. (c) MEASURE IT, DO NOT ASSUME IT: index --with-rows and read pEff at each leg ENTRY (tSeg ~ 0) as a covariate; it is a shipped CSV column. Report the arm effect adjusted for entry pEff, and report the raw one beside it. REQUIREMENT 3, THE PRE-REGISTERED FAILURE SIGNATURE, WHICH MATTERS MORE HERE THAN THE PASS. PASS = per-leg mean pEff rises from 0.466-0.845 toward ~1 on the B arm, WITH terminalOffDeg / rmsPointingErrorDeg / fixedWindowOffDeg improving, AND stickFlipRateP not rising. FAIL-DANGEROUS = the ratchet. Inside a rail-to-rail relay the |cmd| > 0.05 gate closes at every zero crossing (~0.1 s) against a ~1.0 s release tau, so arm B can walk the estimate UP during an oscillation - adding energy to a cycle instead of removing a de-rating. The card must be able to SEE that, so score it two ways: (i) stickFlipRateP and wobbleCoherenceOutP on arm B against arm A on the same tag - any rise is the signature; (ii) from the rows, the within-segment correlation between pEff and the local outP zero-crossing density. A B-arm capture where pEff climbs DURING an oscillation rather than BETWEEN legs is the failure, and it is not visible in a segment mean. REQUIREMENT 4, D1 AND RESPONSIVENESS ARE SEPARATE VERDICTS. Fighter1 inverts the ERROR direction (ledger D7) but does NOT invert the latch (0.656 down / 0.773 up, same sign as the fleet). So a null on the down/up terminalOffDeg RATIO (D1) does not license a null on responsiveness, and a win on responsiveness does not by itself explain D1. Write the two rows in the ledger separately: this arm is a responsiveness hypothesis and only a CANDIDATE mechanism for D1. EFFECT SIZE, COSTED HONESTLY. pErrTerm scales linearly with pEff, so arm B raises the pitch demand by 1/pEff - 1 = +25 pct (Fighter1 up legs, 0.80) to +115 pct (Multirole1 down legs, 0.466) wherever the latch is stuck. Standing error goes roughly as 1/gain, so the predicted elevation-lag improvement is 20-50 pct on the low-pEff lanes - an order above the 1-3 pct cross-batch acceptance band G9 establishes and above the +/-3 pct within-batch replicate scatter. On this geometry that estimate is undiluted; had it been flown on oblique-6-c it would have been ~4x smaller and could have read as a null. FastBomber1 and Darkreach are the near-null lanes by construction (pEff already 0.77-0.85) and are the within-batch control. FALSIFIER. pEff mean rises to ~1 on arm B exactly as designed, and terminalOffDeg / rmsPointingErrorDeg / fixedWindowOffDeg are indistinguishable between arms on every lane and every direction. That says the de-rating is not on the path that decides pointing accuracy, the latch is cosmetic, and the responsiveness complaint is elsewhere - which retires the best hypothesis the project currently has and is worth 13 minutes to learn. MANDATORY EXPOSURE CHECK BEFORE ANY VERDICT: pEff must actually separate between arms. If the A-arm and B-arm per-leg means are within noise, the lever did not fire and nothing else in the card is interpretable. repeat 9 = 4k+1 per X27 (8 scored replicates, 4 per arm, ABBA balanced per lane). count 10 = one lane per key; the arm is per-aircraft since v0.94, so all ten lanes sweep their own independent ABBA and this returns TEN independent A/Bs from one launch.
